summary.text: 白 is the character for “white.” Its earliest graph is pictorial, but the object it depicts is disputed; the familiar shape should not be confidently explained as a candle, sun rays, thumb, or vessel.

formation.text: Pictographic in origin, though its referent is unresolved. One account proposes a thumb; another proposes a cooking or measuring vessel whose middle stroke marks the join between lid and body. Neither is established as consensus, and the later meaning “white” cannot by itself identify the pictured object.

components.text: The whole early graph is treated as one pictorial form. Competing accounts identify it as a thumb or a vessel; the evidence does not establish separate components or settle which object was depicted.

history.text: Curated script-style redrawings show an oracle-bone form with a rounded outline and two interior strokes, a bronze-style form with a pointed upper outline and two interior strokes, and a seal-style form with a taller central stroke and divided body. These are comparative graphic witnesses, not proof of a particular origin or a dated sequence of individual inscriptions.
The seal-script tradition explains 白 as 入 joined with 二, with 二 interpreted as an “yin number.” This is a historical account of the graph, not confirmation of its early pictorial origin.
No sound component is proposed for 白. The dossier reports early uses for the color word 白, 伯, and a place name, but does not establish their order or individually dated first attestations.

uncertainties.text: The early referent remains disputed. The thumb and vessel proposals conflict, and other proposals include cloth, flame or light, and a face or head. The vessel account also cannot establish the ancient name or pronunciation of the object.
The available evidence does not resolve whether the graph was first used for “white,” 伯, or another recorded use; nor does it establish a secure semantic development linking 白 and 百.
Comparative word-etymology proposals for 白 disagree, and neither identifies a sound-bearing component in the graph.

developments.text: A proposed account says the written graph 白 was reused to write 伯 because the words sounded alike. The available evidence supplies no dated phonological argument establishing that match; a competing account links 伯 to a thumb’s supposed leading position instead.

limitations.text: The order of early uses and exact first-attestation dates are unresolved. A reported borrowing for 伯 does not establish that the color sense developed from a depicted object, and no sound for the proposed object is known.
The reported ancient use “hundred” does not establish a semantic transition from “white.”
The evidence lists “pure, unblemished” and “bright” as glosses but gives no dated history connecting them to earlier senses.

overview.text: 白 means “white.” Its early graph was pictorial, but scholars disagree about what it pictured, so its familiar outline does not provide a secure origin story.

components.text: Treat the early form as one picture: the evidence disputes whether it showed a thumb or a vessel.

takeaway.text: The proposed borrowing for 伯 depends on a sound resemblance, but that historical sound link is not established here.
